newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast late products flatten on slow trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast late products flatten on slow trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast products prices continued their flat pattern in late trading on Thursday, with demand weak and NYMEX instability sidelining trade.
"The overall market is on the weak side," one dealer said, noting refineries operated normally, except for a scheduled outage at Chevron's refinery at El Segundo, California.
"They're well-covered," the dealer said, reiterating rumours that Chevron was out of the market and long crude.
Only jet fuel showed strength, as offers rose a half cent a gallon to 70 cents, amid rumours a cargo was loading for export out of Shell's refinery in San Francisco.
Traders said they were not sure if the shipment was bound for PADD 1 East Coast or overseas.
Meanwhile, NYMEX heating oil ended the day 0.73 cent higher at 72.29 cents a gallon, one day after a swing of almost four cents.
The market turned nervous because of concerns about the outcome of a meeting between U.S. energy officials and industry representatives planned for Friday.
The two sides plan to discuss ways to curb the effects of short heating oil stocks in the coming cold months out east.
November parcels for Los Angeles CARB regular gasoline were unchanged at 67/68 cents for the second-straight day.
Conventional regular gasoline in L.A. stayed flat at 62/63 cents.
San Francisco gasoline was 1.50 cents under L.A.
November low sulphur diesel was 70.75/71.75 cents, in line with Wednesday assessments.
November CARB diesel in L.A. was offered at 79 cents, four cents below October parcels, which fell two cents to 81/83 cents on overproduction.
